title: Krasner neighbourhoods over henselian fields of arbitrary valuation rank
statement: Let $F$ be a field with a nontrivial valuation and henselian valuation ring [def-trf-valuation-ring, def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Let $N/F$ be a finite Galois extension: finite, separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], and normal, meaning that every minimal polynomial of an element of $N$ over $F$ splits in $N[T]$. Fix a valuation $w$ of $N$ prolonging that of $F$, with values in a totally ordered abelian group, written additively. For $\alpha,\beta\in N$, suppose that $w(\alpha-\beta)>w(\alpha-\sigma(\alpha))$ for every $\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}_F(N)$ with $\sigma(\alpha)\ne\alpha$. Then $\alpha\in F(\beta)$, where $F(\beta)$ is the smallest subfield containing $F$ and $\beta$ [def-pc-field-extension]. Thus there is an open neighbourhood $U$ of $\alpha$ in $N$ such that every $\beta\in U$ satisfies $\alpha\in F(\beta)$. When $\alpha\in F$ the condition is empty and one may take $U=N$. No completeness or rank restriction is imposed. Here an additive valuation has $w(0)=\infty$, $w(x)\in\Gamma$ for $x\ne0$, $w(xy)=w(x)+w(y)$ and $w(x+y)\geq\min\{w(x),w(y)\}$; its topology has the balls $\{x:w(x-a)>\gamma\}$, $a\in N$, $\gamma\in\Gamma$, as a basis. Its valuation ring is $\mathcal O_w=\{x:w(x)\geq0\}$.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.374, forms of Krasner lemma, reference to Bourbaki, Algebre commutative VI section 8 exercises 12 and 14(a). Stacks Tag 09EI only treats a complete one-dimensional local domain, and is not a source for the unrestricted-rank statement.

proof.text: Put $G=\operatorname{Aut}_F(N)$ and $W=\mathcal O_w$. For $\sigma\in G$, $w\circ\sigma$ is another prolongation of the given valuation on $F$. Apply the uniqueness clause of [lem-per-henselian-finite-extension-topology] with $E=N$: its hypotheses are exactly the nontrivial valuation, henselian valuation ring and finite algebraic extension assumed here. Thus $\sigma^{-1}W=W$, so $\sigma$ preserves $W$ and its units.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed pp.373–374 (PDF pp.379–380), valued-field paragraph; agent reconstruction of the Krasner argument referred to there.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-fixed-field], $G$ is finite. Hence each $\sigma\in G$ has finite order $r>0$: two powers coincide and cancellation gives $\sigma^r=1$. For nonzero $a,b$, $w(a)>w(b)$ means $a/b\in W\setminus W^\times$, which the preceding step shows is preserved by $\sigma$. If $w(\sigma x)>w(x)$, applying this observation repeatedly gives $w(x)<w(\sigma x)<\cdots<w(\sigma^r x)=w(x)$, a contradiction; the reverse strict inequality gives a decreasing contradiction. Therefore $w(\sigma x)=w(x)$ for every $x\ne0$, and also for $x=0$.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed pp.373–374 (PDF pp.379–380), valued-field paragraph; agent reconstruction of the Krasner argument referred to there.

proof.text: Let $H\subseteq G$ consist of the automorphisms fixing $F(\beta)$ pointwise. For $\tau\in H$ we have $\tau\beta=\beta$, so $\alpha-\tau\alpha=(\alpha-\beta)-\tau(\alpha-\beta)$. The valuation axioms and the preceding equality give $w(\alpha-\tau\alpha)\geq\min\{w(\alpha-\beta),w(\tau(\alpha-\beta))\}=w(\alpha-\beta)$. If $\tau\alpha\ne\alpha$, this contradicts the strict inequality in the hypothesis. Hence every element of $H$ fixes $\alpha$. This calculation also covers $\alpha=\beta$, with $w(0)=\infty$.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed pp.373–374 (PDF pp.379–380), valued-field paragraph; agent reconstruction of the Krasner argument referred to there.

proof.text: Apply the finite Galois fixed-field theorem IsGalois.fixedField_fixingSubgroup, the finite specialization of [lem-exc-etale-galois-fixed-field-subgroup], to N/F and F(beta). The ultrametric calculation proves that every member of its fixing subgroup fixes alpha, so alpha belongs to F(beta).

source.place: XX 4.4, printed pp.373–374 (PDF pp.379–380), valued-field paragraph; agent reconstruction of the Krasner argument referred to there.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-fixed-field], the automorphism group G is finite. Let S be the subtype of automorphisms moving alpha. For each sigma in S, alpha - sigma(alpha) is nonzero, so its additive valuation is a finite value gamma_sigma in the ambient ordered group. Let U be the intersection over S of the basic open balls {beta : gamma_sigma < w(beta - alpha)}. This finite intersection is open and contains alpha, since w(0) is infinity. Symmetry w(beta-alpha)=w(alpha-beta) shows every beta in U satisfies all Krasner inequalities, so the preceding steps give alpha in F(beta). If alpha lies in the base field, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-fixed-field] says that every automorphism fixes alpha; then S is empty and U=N. This avoids choosing a maximum or requiring a moving conjugate; it also handles N=F and alpha=beta without a separate case.

lean.statement: theorem henselian_krasner_neighbourhood {F : Type u} [Field F] {N : Type v} [Field N] [Algebra F N] [FiniteDimensional F N] [IsGalois F N] {Γ : Type w} [AddCommGroup Γ] [LinearOrder Γ] [IsOrderedAddMonoid Γ] (vF : AddValuation F (WithTop Γ)) [vF.toValuation.IsNontrivial] [HenselianLocalRing vF.toValuation.integer] (wN : AddValuation N (WithTop Γ)) (hw : wN.comap (algebraMap F N) = vF) (α : N) : (∀ β : N, (∀ σ : N ≃ₐ[F] N, σ α ≠ α → wN (α - σ α) < wN (α - β)) → α ∈ IntermediateField.adjoin F {β}) ∧ ∃ U : Set N, @IsOpen N (TopologicalSpace.generateFrom {B : Set N | ∃ a : N, ∃ γ : Γ, B = {x : N | (γ : WithTop Γ) < wN (x - a)}}) U ∧ α ∈ U ∧ (∀ β ∈ U, α ∈ IntermediateField.adjoin F {β}) ∧ (α ∈ Set.range (algebraMap F N) → U = Set.univ)
